Claude B moved it to `WaypointKit/Sources/WaypointKit/LedgerValueModifiers.swift` as `public`, and left the app-target file as an inert pointer comment rather than deleting it outright (avoids a dangling `project.pbxproj` reference, correctly left for me to clean up if I chose to — I didn't need to, since the file itself is unchanged in the project graph, just its contents). I confirmed `TripLiveActivity.swift` already `import WaypointKit` and calls `.ledgerValueStyle()` at line 93 — this should resolve cleanly. Both Claude A and Claude B independently converged on the identical fix and correctly avoided duplicating it.

It correctly implements the free-tier gate as a pure count check, explicitly avoids the "active trip" naming collision `[REDACTED:high_entropy]` called out, and is honestly *not* wired into `TripSwitcherView`'s "New Trip" button yet — that's flagged as separate future work (upsell copy, `isPro` plumbing) rather than rushed in.

**Nothing to wire this round:** `LedgerValueModifiers.swift` (new, WaypointKit), `TripGateChecker.swift`, and `TripGateCheckerTests.swift` all sit in SwiftPM auto-globbed paths — no `Package.swift` or `project.pbxproj` edits needed.

CONSENSUS: YES

The reported compile blocker is fixed at the source: the ledger-value text style now lives in the shared `WaypointKit` package so both the main app and the widget/Live Activity extension can see it, matching the same cross-target-sharing pattern already used for `Theme`/`DemoStampBadge`/`CategoryPin`. On top of that, this round closed the last known missing piece from the monetization gate — `TripGateChecker` is now real code with real tests, though still (correctly, honestly) not wired into any UI button yet. Test coverage across the project now includes the free-tier trip-count gate alongside everything from the previous round (atomic cross-day reorder, trip date-range math, settlement split arithmetic, the debug date-injection hook, the shrink-guard).

**To run it:** open `Waypoint.xcodeproj` in Xcode 16+, scheme `Waypoint`, and either run the app on an iOS 17+ simulator or run Tests (⌘U). I cannot personally confirm a green compile from this environment — `xcodebuild`/`swift build` both require interactive approval that isn't available in this session — so build_verification's next run against the real toolchain is still the first actual confirmation this fix works, not just a from-my-side "should work."
